reasons.reason: There's no native SMS: texting only works once you connect and pay for your own Twilio account, since systeme.io publishes no messaging rate of its own.

picks.why: Prices SMS at $0.01 per outbound US segment inside the same platform as email, with carrier fees already included in that rate, so texting is billed and sent from one account instead of a second one you open and fund yourself.

reasons.reason: Product variants are capped at 50, 100 or 250 depending on plan, and even the plans API behind the $97 Unlimited tier still stops at 5,000 despite the pricing page calling that limit unlimited, so a real physical-product catalog needs a dedicated commerce back office.

picks.why: Every plan allows unlimited products, and Shopify adds no transaction fee at all once a store uses Shopify Payments, removing the ceiling systeme.io's funnel-first catalog was never built to lift.
The core plugin is free with no item cap and no revenue share, so a growing catalog is limited only by hosting, never by a plan tier.

reasons.reason: Startup's own limits show up fast: 10 tags, 10 automation rules and 10 sales funnels, tight the moment a list or its sequences grow past a beginner setup.

picks.why: Every paid plan, including the entry tier billed at $15 a month annually, bundles marketing automation and a light CRM with no fixed count of tags, rules or funnels to bump against.

reasons.reason: The course tool is one feature inside a funnel builder, not a dedicated platform, so a business built around courses, coaching and community outgrows it once campaigns and pages need to run with no cap at all.

picks.why: Landing pages, funnels and marketing emails are unlimited on every plan, including the entry-level Basic plan, and a 30-day money-back guarantee covers a tier that turns out to be the wrong fit.

reasons.reason: Running several client accounts turns into several capped accounts, not several separate allowances, since every sub-account simply inherits its parent plan's own tags, funnels and automation-rule limits.

picks.why: Sub-accounts carry their own CRM and phone system rather than inheriting a parent plan's funnel and automation caps, and every plan includes unlimited users and contacts.
